hypotheses.claim: A finite declared relation/predicate registry resolved into typed canonical IR can retain selected readable G9 word-relations while failing closed on undeclared relation words, without adding new cognitive/runtime semantics.
support: 0/50000 unknown relation words accepted by strict resolver
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Normalize all prose-like relation forms to calls/punctuation/qualified fields; a relation registry adds unnecessary parser/type-system complexity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Full-current-corpus parser/roundtrip/cost benchmark shows declared relation resolution is ambiguous, less stable, or materially more expensive than normalization.

hypotheses.claim: Declared relation words should live in a typed semantic symbol/operation registry rather than lexer-only keyword accretion, so surface readability does not mint meaning or authority.
support: Tree-sitter official docs separate keyword/identifier lexical handling and contextual lexing
MLIR ODS/SymbolTable use explicit operation/symbol definitions with verification
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Lexer-level reserved keywords alone are sufficient and simpler.
hypotheses.falsifier: A complete parser with lexer-only relation keywords preserves intended AST, diagnostics, symbol evolution and semantic hashes with lower complexity and no accidental acceptance.

hypotheses.claim: The concurrent strict-normalization policy may still be superior to declared relation words if it lowers repair cost and parser ambiguity across the full G9 corpus.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Selective declared relations preserve equivalent determinism with lower migration/edit cost and better model/human readability.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched full-corpus and reader/compiler benchmark decisively favors one policy on parse closure, roundtrip stability, diagnostics, migration burden and target-reader performance.
